findings.area: run() + geomkit.dedupe (pre-existing; reached through the mapping 'units' input)
findings.summary: dedupe() rounds the RAW cache coordinates to 3 decimals before the unit scale is applied, so its resolution is 1 mm only for units 'mm': 1 cm for 'cm', 2.5 cm for 'in', 0.3 m for 'ft', 1 m for 'm'. Distinct face lines and pieces collapse into 'duplicates', walls vanish, openings are lost or invented, silently. In cm / in it also merges the 5-30 mm faces the new thin-screen rule (3) needs.
findings.repro: units_repro.py: two 4 m walls drawn as face LINEs 0.2 m apart, 1.2 m gap, back wall: units mm / cm / in give the passage, units m and ft give [] (orig and merged); with dedupe off every unit gives the passage. End to end with the real CLI: ME/cli_units holds bank1 with every coordinate x0.001 and a mapping with units 'm': cd ME/detector && OPENINGS_DATA=ME/cli_units/data python -B openings.py ME/cli_units/maps/bank1_m.json out.json gives 24 openings that are not the mm run's openings (4-5 differ). units_real.py bank1 l29 presidential: m: bank L1 5 differ, L29 6 differ (Sukhumvit ground 31 openings instead of 43); ft: L29 2 differ; in: presidential 1 differ.

findings.area: screen_doors -> strip_gaps (patch 3): new quadratic call site
findings.summary: screen_doors runs strip_gaps on every thin glass strip. strip_gaps has two pure-Python double loops (gaps x strips with ang_diff at ~10 us per pair, and the gap de-duplication); all thin strips pass the abs(S.t - g.t) > 0.04 pre-test, so cost is ~(4N)(2N) pairs. Real drawings have at most 10 thin strips so today it costs 0.01-0.03 s, but a floor with hundreds of glass partitions hits it.

findings.suggestedFix: In the collinear-strip loop of strip_gaps pre-filter with numpy per gap (|t - g.t| <= 0.04, |u.g.u| >= cos 2 deg, |lateral offset of g.b| <= 0.03) and run the exact tests on the survivors only (identical gap lists on L30 x10); in the de-dup loop test the distances before ang_diff.
